This petition is filed by the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 6 under Section 528 of BNSS 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing criminal proceedings in CC.No.9529/2024 in Crime No.83/2023 registered by the Kalaburagi women Police station,
Kalaburagi and charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 498A, 504, 506 read with 34 of IPC and sections 3 and 4 of DP Act, pending on I Addl. CJ and JMFC, Gulbarga.
2.

entities.text: I Addl. CJ and JMFC, Gulbarga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioners, learned HCGP for the State and learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
3. The case of the prosecution is that on the complaint filed by the respondent No.2 to the police on 28.6.2023, the police registered FIR.

It is alleged that she is working in the Excise Department,
Bengaluru and she was married to petitioner No.1 on 21.2.2021.
As per the demand, her father had given 24 tolas of gold and Rs.5 lakhs as dowry and by spending Rs.25 lakhs for the marriage.

After the marriage, the NC: 2024:KHC-K:8181 accused No.1 and herself were residing at Bengaluru,
previously 2 months they had resided at Kalaburagi.
At that time, they said to have harassed her physically and mentally by abusing her in filthy languages and they demanded Rs.10 lakhs as additional dowry.
Therefore, she managed to give Rs.4 lakhs by cash, but later they demanded another Rs.6 lakhs and they said to be assaulted and abused her.
Therefore, she got her job transferred to Kalaburagi and because of non-toleration of harassment, she has filed the complaint before the police.
The police after registering the FIR, investigated the matter and filed the charge sheet, which is under challenge.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended, there is no specific allegations against any of the accused persons.
The accused No.1 and complainant were married and stayed at Bengaluru in Nagarbhavi for 7 months separately not with the family members.
The accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents.

Accused No.4 is his brother and accused No.5 is the wife of accused No.4 and accused No.7 is another married sister, they are all residing separately and not resided together with the accused No.1 and respondent No.2, at any point of time.

Even though there is no demand of dowry, but the respondent No.2 NC: 2024:KHC-K:8181 is having illegal intimacy with her colleague in Excise Department and when the same was questioned she was reluctant and transferred to some other district, Bengaluru to Kalaburagi.
The respondent accused No.1 filed divorce case against the respondent No.2 for cruelty, as well as adultery under Section 13(1)(i)(a) of Hindu Marriage Act.
She has appeared and filed written statement.
She has not stated any allegation for dowry harassment.

sentences.text: The accused No.1 also lead evidence and at that time, this complaint came to be filed only to harass the petitioner and as a counter blast.
Therefore, it is contended there is a telephonic conversation and photographs were used to show she is having intimacy with another person which was named in the divorce petition.
Therefore, continuing the proceedings is nothing but abuse of process of law.
Hence, prayed for allowing this petition and quashing the criminal proceedings.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 seriously objected the petition contending that all the accused persons seriously harassed the victim girl by demanding dowry and accepting the golden ornaments.
Apart from that, they demanded further dowry of Rs.10 lakhs and received Rs.4 NC: 2024:KHC-K:8181 lakhs.
Such being the case, question of quashing the criminal proceedings does not arises.
Hence, prayed for rejecting the petition.

6. Having heard the arguments, perused the records which reveals ofcourse, the marriage between the petitioner No.1 and the respondent No.2 is not in dispute, where it is alleged that the golden ornaments and cash was given by her father.
Subsequent to the marriage, both accused No.1 and the respondent No.2 had resided at Bengaluru where the respondent No.2 is working in Excise Department as official at Bengaluru.
Therefore, she resided along with accused No.1 in a separate house.
Subsequently she got transferred to Kalaburagi and thereafter almost after two and half years this complaint came to be filed.

It is also seen from the record, the counsel for petitioner produced the copy of the divorce petition where the petitioner No.1 alleged against respondent No.2 on adultery ground for granting divorce.
He also made respondent No.2 as the adulterer as party in the divorce petition.
The divorce petition came to be filed on 04.08.2021, immediately 7 months after the marriage.
The respondent No.2 appeared in the family court, she also filed statement of objection by taking NC: 2024:KHC-K:8181 various contention.
Thereafter, the evidence of the petitioner No.1 was let in the family court where he has made same allegation of adultery in his evidence.

7. The evidence of the PW1 i.e., accused No.1 has been deferred and subsequently the cross examination was commenced on 03.07.2023 in the intervening period i.e., between examination chief and cross examination, the respondent No.2 went to the Police station on 28.6.2023 filed a complaint.

Thereafter, started cross examination of the PW1 i.e, petitioner/accused No.1 and by taking various contention in the cross examination, which clearly reveals this complaint came to be filed only as a counter blast to the divorce petition filed by the accused No.1, on the ground of adultery and cruelty.

The learned counsel has rightly contended that if at all any cruelty or harassment, the respondent No.2 could have filed complaint immediately in the year 2021 itself,
when she got transferred to Kalaburagi from Bengaluru.
But it appears filing of the complaint orally after examination chief lead by the accused No.1 in the family court and prior to cross examination as a counter blast.

Whatever the contention taken by the complainant in the complaint is nothing but a omnibus NC: 2024:KHC-K:8181 allegation made against the entire family members that altogether they harassed and demanded dowry and there is inordinate delay of 2 years in filing the complaint against the petitioners, except after examination of the accused No.1 in the family court as witnesses by producing the various documents especially the CDR records, reveals there is a conversation between the respondent No.2 and accused No.1 and others which reveals this complaint is filed only as a counter blast to take revenge against the petitioners.

Accordingly, this petition is allowed.
The criminal proceedings against the petitioners in CC.No.9529/2024 in Crime No.83/2023 registered by the Kalaburagi women Police station Kalaburagi, pending on I Addl.

CJ and JMFC,
Gulbarga, is hereby quashed.
The family court dealing with the divorce case shall not influence any of the observations made by this court in this case.
